01 / YOUR PRACTICE RUN

Your first exam experience?
Have it on the sofa.

Kanjidon has JLPT mock exams for all five levels, N5 to N1, with Premium. Sections and timing follow the test structure: language knowledge, reading and listening. The timer runs, you move between sections, and you learn to pace yourself before facing the real answer sheet.

You can try, get things wrong, understand why and try again. That mistake stays out of your official result. The mocks use preparation questions created for Kanjidon, helping you get comfortable with the JLPT format and what lies ahead.

Why do N2 and N1 have a combined cell? That’s how the JLPT works: vocabulary, grammar and reading share one block of 105 minutes for N2 or 110 for N1. Listening is separate. At N5, N4 and N3, vocabulary has its own time slot, separate from grammar and reading. Knowing the difference helps you practise at the right pace.

Got something wrong? Now you know where to start.

After the mock, pick three things to revisit: a tough section, a recurring mistake, something that ate up your time. Work on those topics in Kanjidon, then test yourself again. Start with one thing you can improve; everything else can follow.

Track progress by section as well as overall. The mock’s percentage helps you follow your practice; the JLPT uses scaled scores, with overall and sectional pass marks. How official scoring works ↗

Why Kanjidon helps right now

When time is tight, deciding where to start each day is tiring in itself. Kanjidon brings the mock and your preparation tools together: exams, cards, lessons and review. Find a difficulty, work on it, then put it to the test. That connection makes it a useful companion on the way to the JLPT.

02 / TAKE BACK CONTROL

Stop trying to review everything.
Start with what you need.

Building your preparation around Kanjidon keeps things connected: cards give you material to review, lessons add context, and mock exams put your work to the test.

01

Take your first mock

Open the level you registered for and give it a go. Even if you don’t feel ready yet: finding your focus is the whole point. You don’t have to know everything before you start.

02

Review to remember

Use cards and quizzes to recall the answer before revealing it. Spaced repetition (SRS) schedules review over time. A kanji you recognise today needs to stick around next week too.

03

Put it all to the test

Take a mock and notice where you lose ground: vocabulary, grammar, reading or listening. Start your next study block there, rather than with the chapter you already know inside out.

03 / ONE STEP AT A TIME

From “Where do I even start?”
to “Here’s what I’m doing today.”

Let’s organise the time you have left. Fit these five stages around your schedule: a first mock, focused work, regular practice exams and final review. Fewer weeks available? Prioritise the difficulties your mock reveals.

N3 · Connect the details

Work on connections between sentences, grammar nuances and sustained listening. Alternate card review, lessons and comprehension practice.

Allow 140 minutes for a full mock, plus time to review it.
  1. START HERE

    Break the ice.

    Start with your level’s Kanjidon mock, available with Premium. Note your three main obstacles and give each some space in your week. Your first result is a starting point. You’re allowed to still be practising.

    Goal: know what to work on.
  2. THE FIRST FEW WEEKS

    Build your routine.

    Review in Kanjidon most days, take lessons on shakier topics, and read and listen regularly. Add cards at a pace you can keep reviewing. At the end of the week, check whether recurring mistakes are becoming less frequent.

    Goal: strengthen the foundations you need.
  3. FIND YOUR PACE

    Start the timer.

    Schedule a full mock every week or two, depending on your time. Set aside another session to review it. On other days, work on the difficulties in Kanjidon and practise reading within a time limit.

    Goal: answer more accurately within the time.
  4. TWO WEEKS BEFORE THE EXAM

    Have a dress rehearsal.

    Try a mock without interruptions within each section. Add official samples or practice workbooks to get familiar with instructions and the answer sheet. Let your mistakes guide review, instead of switching methods every other day.

    Goal: feel familiar with the exam format.
  5. THE FINAL WEEK

    Turn down the volume. You’ve put in the work.

    Keep Kanjidon reviews short, revisit mistakes you’ve resolved and notice how far you’ve come. Go easy on new cards and make room for sleep. You can close the app on the last evening: arriving rested is part of preparing too.

    Goal: arrive clear-headed and confident in your work.

04 / LET’S CLEAR THINGS UP

“Okay, but one more question…”

Not much time, cards to unlock, that slightly daunting first mock. Let’s talk.

Short on time: can I unlock all my level’s cards straight away?

Absolutely! Kanjidon’s store lets you unlock the cards for your level and start reviewing right away, without waiting to find them in packs. Want mock exams too? Look at bundles combining cards and Premium. There’s also a complete bundle.

The cards-only option unlocks the material; Premium gives you access to mock exams. The app shows each offer’s contents, price and duration so you can choose what suits you and get started.

How close are the mocks to the real JLPT?

They let you practise its format: sections and timing follow your level’s test, including listening. Questions are Kanjidon exercises designed for preparation. You get used to the pace, learn to manage the minutes and discover how to approach each part. Add official samples and the answer sheet to round out your rehearsal.

Are there mock exams for my level?

Yes: N5, N4, N3, N2 and N1. All of them! Pick yours in the app and start there. Whether you’re building foundations or exploring complex texts, you can combine mocks with review and lessons on your path.

What can I practise besides kanji?

Vocabulary, grammar, reading and listening: every area you meet in the JLPT. Cards help kanji stick, lessons put them in context, and mocks bring your work together. Seeing the things you’ve studied click together is the good part.

I have twenty minutes. How can I use them?

Open Kanjidon’s reviews and pick a small goal: a few cards, a grammar point or a short listening exercise. Twenty focused minutes can keep you moving even on busy days. Book a longer slot for a full mock, perhaps at the weekend: your own exam rehearsal appointment.

I keep forgetting one card. How do I make it stick?

That card is playing hard to get! Revisit it in Kanjidon’s smart review and connect it to a word or sentence that stays with you. Then try recalling it without looking. When it finally clicks, enjoy it: those little wins make you want to keep going.

I passed a mock. Am I on the right track for the JLPT?

Nice work. Give yourself credit! You tackled a test at your level and passed it: that’s something to build confidence on. Notice your strongest sections and review those that need a little polish. Repeating good performances within the time gives you more concrete signs that your work is coming together. Take that confidence with you: your progress is showing.

How do I bounce back after a rough mock?

With a small comeback. Pick a couple of tricky questions, revisit the topics in Kanjidon and give yourself time to understand them. In the next mock, look for what now feels easier too. Preparation is made of these steps forward. And yes, they’re worth celebrating even while there’s more to work on.

LESS “WHAT IF”. MORE “I’M WORKING ON IT”.
